name: GPT Workspace
tagline: An AI sidebar and spreadsheet formulas that put a chat model inside Google Docs, Sheets, Slides and Gmail.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a wrapper: it takes text you selected or cells you referenced, sends them to a model API, and writes the answer back into the document. Google already ships the runtime you need, Apps Script, which can add sidebars to Docs and Slides, custom functions to Sheets, and menu items to Gmail drafts, all with a single fetch call to whatever model you like. One session gets you a working sidebar plus a spreadsheet function that fills a column, running on your own API key with no subscription in the middle. The gaps are polish and breadth, not capability: quota ceilings on Sheets custom functions, the unverified-app scare screen, and the fact that every extra surface is another chunk of UI you now maintain. The value here is convenience, and convenience is exactly the thing an agent is good at reproducing.
coreLoopDIY: A personal Apps Script add-on that adds an AI sidebar to Docs and Slides and a spreadsheet function that runs prompts over cell ranges using your own model API key.
requirements: A model API key, OpenAI or Anthropic or a local server
A Google account with Apps Script enabled
Node and clasp if you want to edit code locally instead of in the browser
Tolerance for Google's unverified-app consent screen on first run
whatYouLose: A polished, consistent UI across Docs, Sheets, Slides, Gmail and Drive instead of the two or three surfaces you actually finish
Sheets custom functions in Apps Script are quota-limited and time out, so bulk column fills need batching you have to write yourself
Prompt libraries, templates and saved presets that make the paid version feel fast on day one
Domain-wide install and billing for a team, plus admin key management; yours is per account, per script
Someone else fixing it when Google changes add-on authorization rules again
moatNotes: The integration surface is Google's, not theirs, which is also why anyone can build on it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the paid version is already installed, already covers five apps, and already has a prompt menu that someone thought about. Buying it takes two minutes and no API key; a team of ten does not want ten Apps Script projects and ten billing accounts at OpenAI. There is also a real support burden here that a personal build hides: Google periodically tightens add-on scopes and authorization flows, and someone has to keep up with that. For one person who mostly wants AI in a spreadsheet, none of that justifies a recurring bill.
notes: The rare case where the incumbent's platform is also the DIY platform, which is not a great place to be selling from.
prompt:
Build a personal Google Workspace add-on that puts an AI assistant inside my own documents. Stack: Google Apps Script, deployed as a test editor add-on from a standalone script project, edited locally with clasp and TypeScript-free plain JS. No separate backend, no hosting, no accounts.

Project layout in this folder:
- appsscript.json declaring an editor add-on for Docs, Sheets and Slides, plus the script.external_request scope
- Code.js with the onOpen and onInstall triggers for all three hosts
- Sidebar.html served with HtmlService, one file, inline CSS, no build step
- Llm.js with a single callModel(prompt, systemPrompt) function using UrlFetchApp
- README.md with the exact clasp commands and the test-deployment steps

Features, in scope:
1. Sidebar in Docs and Slides: a prompt box, a model picker with two hardcoded options, a Run button, and buttons to Insert, Replace selection, or just Copy the result.
2. Sidebar reads the current selection as context when there is one, otherwise the whole document body truncated to a sane character budget.
3. Four fixed quick actions: Rewrite clearer, Summarize, Translate to English, Fix grammar. Hardcode the prompts in a PROMPTS object so I can edit them.
4. A Sheets custom function AI(prompt, range) that concatenates the range as context and returns one cell of text, plus a menu item Fill column that iterates a selected range with batching, a short sleep between calls, and writes results into the next column. Explain in the README that custom functions have a 30 second ceiling and that Fill column is the reliable path.
5. Errors surface as a visible message in the sidebar and as a string starting with ERROR: in cells. Never fail silently.

Out of scope: Gmail, Drive, prompt history, streaming, images, sharing with other users, publishing to the Marketplace, any analytics.

Secrets: store the API key in Script Properties under MODEL_API_KEY. Add a menu item Set API key that prompts for it and saves it. Never hardcode a key and never log it. Include a .env.example only to document the key name for local reference.

When done, print the exact steps: clasp login, clasp create as a standalone script, clasp push, then Deploy as test deployment, then open a document and authorize through the unverified-app screen.
